grand_strategy.reading:
South Korea is a middle power that has turned itself into something every
great power needs - memory chips, shipyards, reactors, howitzers - and has
then discovered that being needed is not the same as being secure. Luttwak's
reading is of an alliance that pays for its own guarantor: the 1953 treaty
and 28,500 soldiers remain the fact on which everything rests, but since
2025 the guarantor sets a price in tariffs, investment pledges, weapons
purchases and support payments, cuts the allied exercises on its own
initiative to court the adversary, and moves air-defence batteries to another
theatre. Seoul answers with the only strategic move open to a rich dependent:
make itself more useful (MASGA, the USD 350bn fund) and more autonomous
(nuclear submarines, enrichment, wartime control) at once, which are
contradictory signals to a guarantor. On the other front stands a deterrence
facing an adversary that has stopped talking: Pyongyang has replaced hostility
to be negotiated with a border to be built, with Russian money and combat
experience behind it, and Lee's outreach - loudspeakers off, regret for drones,
a proposal to end the war - meets a wall of mines and silence. The restoration
of ties with China and Japan in 2026 is the third leg: a hedge, not an
alignment, and the one that Beijing's own Wang Yi describes as 'strategic
autonomy'. Signals that do not fit a row: Putin's January 2026 wish to
'restore ties' and Seoul's ambassador at Vladivostok, while the Hyundai
option on its St Petersburg plant lapsed; and the disclosure of two North
Korean prisoners transferred from Ukraine, which turned Kyiv from a cause into
a quarrel in September-October 2026.

stances.note: The ontology's test is whether Seoul's declared aim is the other's defeat or disappearance, and it is not: the Lee government's line is that Seoul respects the North's system, seeks no unification by absorption and commits no hostile acts (Unification Ministry, per PISM), has silenced the loudspeakers, expressed official regret for civilian drone flights, and proposed talks to formally end the war (15 Aug 2026). The hostility is real but it is on Pyongyang's side: Kim's 'hostile states' doctrine (Dec 2023), the Ninth Party Congress (Feb 2026), a border being fortified and crossed (about 20 MDL crossings in August, 30 in September, mines south of the line, a blast on 21 Sep that hurt three soldiers). Even Pyongyang's March 2026 constitution avoids calling the South an enemy by name (38 North), so 'adversary' would claim a mortal enmity that neither side's written aims state. 'Rival', then, with the trend cooling because the other side keeps closing doors. No source uses the word 'rival': the grade is our reading of the structure (confidence C), like Kosovo's toward Serbia. Bond - kin: one nation divided, which is why the pair is a feud (kin plus rival) in the faults grid.

stances.note: Treaty ally (Mutual Defense Treaty of 1 Oct 1953; 28,500 US troops, a floor written into the FY2026 NDAA; wartime operational control still American). Cooling because the guarantor now charges for the guarantee: a 25%-to-15% tariff deal bought with a USD 350bn pledge (USD 150bn shipbuilding, USD 200bn strategic sectors; first projects 30 Sep 2026), USD 25bn of US arms and USD 33bn for USFK support in the 14 Nov 2025 fact sheet, repeated tariff threats (Jan and Sep 2026), Patriot batteries moved to the Middle East, and Ulchi Freedom Shield cut short by Trump without warning to Seoul. Against that, the fact sheet approved Korean nuclear-powered submarines and backs a path to civil enrichment; the nuclear talks opened on 2-3 Jun 2026. Reluctant ally was considered; no source calls it that and Seoul's own line is a 'comprehensive alliance', so the friction is carried by the trend. Bond - affinity: the 1950-53 war and seven decades of dependence.

stances_toward.note: Rival, not adversary - argued. For: Kim calls South Korea the 'most hostile' state and 'principal enemy', threatens to 'completely destroy' it if threatened, has cut roads and rails, fortified the line since 2024 and has made the doctrine constitutional. Against: the ontology reserves 'adversary' for a declared aim of the other's defeat or disappearance, and the doctrine of December 2023 says the opposite - Pyongyang gave up absorbing the South, wrote reunification out of the constitution (March 2026), defines the South as a bordering state and seeks separation, the destruction threat being conditional on attack. A state that fences itself off and denies the other state's claim to kinship is a rival with an arms race, not a mortal enemy; Seoul's own 'peaceful two-state' white paper (May 2026) treats it the same way. Cooling because the 2025-26 steps (Party Congress, border works, mines of 21 Sep 2026, rejection of every Seoul overture by Kim Yo Jong and the SPA speech) hardened the separation, not because of any thaw. Bond - kin: language, history and the 1948 founding claim; Pyongyang formally repudiates it, so the pair is a feud in Luttwak's sense and Pyongyang's repudiation is the bet, not yet the fact. The USA-PRK pair below is the real test of adversary and stays rival too.

relations_to.summary: KF-21 co-development: Indonesia agreed in 2015 to pay 20% of the cost (KRW 1.6-1.7 trillion), fell behind, and Seoul cut its share to KRW 600 billion with less technology transfer; DAPA says the contribution was paid (June), a prototype transfer is tentatively agreed and a purchase of about 16 aircraft is under discussion.
relations_to.note: The original pledge is reported as KRW 1.6 trillion (Defense Post) or 1.7 trillion (others); the revised KRW 600 billion is reported consistently. Dollar conversions vary (USD 387m to 437m).

relations_to.summary: Constitution revised in March 2026 to define the territory as the land bordering China and Russia to the north and South Korea to the south and to remove all references to reunification; the president of the State Affairs Commission takes command of nuclear forces. Follows Kim's December 2023 - January 2024 declaration of South Korea as the 'primary foe and invariable principal enemy'. The Ninth Congress (Feb 2026) called South Korea the 'most hostile' state and ruled out all dealings.
relations_to.note: The adoption date is reported variously (March 2026 per Yonhap; one analysis points to the October 2024 SPA session); the Yonhap/Korea Herald date of May 2026 reporting is used.

relations_to.summary: Border severance and fortification since 2024: roads and rails cut, barbed-wire fences within 80 metres of the line, mines cleared and laid 5-10 metres from it, about 5,000 troops mobilised in the first half of 2026 (about 1,000 a year earlier); Seoul expects completion around 2028 and says only about 250 of the 1,292 line markers remain. Seoul says the work violates the 1953 armistice; the UN Command takes a more cautious line.

relations_to.summary: Two mines detonated along the line on 21 Sep 2026; Seoul's defence minister said they were deliberately planted by the North, and Kim Yo Jong called the assessment a 'conspiratorial farce', threatening retaliation if the South fires on troops doing the work. Seoul counts about 30 crossings of the line in September.
